76896.subject: The TradeXYZ Question
76896.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/eaa70932-7ce4-467e-b338-a662ed575d6a/0xR_NL_Banner_Heading_Wordmark.jpg?t=1776775276)
Caption: 

———————————————————————————

Markets are becoming more selective. AI spending is being rewarded only where it produces growth without crushing cash flow, while crypto continues to face ETF outflows and rising yields.

Within crypto, leadership rotated toward Solana and DEXs. We also examine the growing debate around TradeXYZ, Hyperliquid, and how value from HIP-3 is ultimately shared.

———————————————————————————

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/42e942ec-f31d-4957-8722-a3ac7b121e1e/0xR_NL_Market_Update.png?t=1767631151) [Market Update]
Caption: 

Over the last week, performance across the major benchmarks was mixed. The S&P 500 and Gold posted modest gains of 0.74% and 0.65% respectively, while the Nasdaq finished broadly flat. BTC was the weakest performer, ending the week down -3.0%.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/39fab82e-204d-4b8a-a0ea-ae85b06bcf84/image.png?t=1785741307)
Caption: 

Last week also brought a wave of earnings from the AI heavyweights. Amazon [surged](https://www.reuters.com/business/nasdaq-100-leads-us-futures-higher-amazon-surge-offsets-apple-decline-2026-07-31/) more than 15% after delivering its strongest quarterly revenue growth in over four years, with AWS revenue rising 37% year over year to $42.2B. Microsoft also gained more than 15% after [reporting](https://www.reuters.com/business/microsoft-set-record-one-day-market-cap-gain-after-upbeat-azure-forecast-2026-07-30/) stronger than expected cloud growth while guiding to lower capital expenditures than Wall Street had anticipated. In contrast, Meta [fell](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/29/meta-q2-earnings-report-2026.html) 10% after second quarter free cash flow dropped 91% as higher AI related capital expenditure weighed on profitability. One theme has become increasingly clear this earnings season. Markets are no longer rewarding AI spending alone. They are rewarding companies that can demonstrate returns on those investments without sacrificing cash flow.

Crypto, meanwhile, continued to face headwinds. ETF flows turned negative once again, with BTC and ETH ETFs recording net outflows of $255M and $69M respectively. Risk sentiment has also been pressured by the bond market, with the US 30 year Treasury yield climbing to [5.23%](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/US30Y), its highest level since June 2007.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/2163d9a1-8a5e-41e9-bf17-3203838a93c6/image.png?t=1785741307)
Caption: 

Within crypto, leadership rotated once again

Enjoying this newsletter? Get it in your inbox every weekend, as well as our daily round-up of The Economist’s best journalism, by signing up for free here. In the 2000s and 2010s millions of American jobs were destroyed by automation and Chinese competition. Now AI threatens to do the same. In theory innovation and change create just as many new jobs as they wipe out—but getting old workers into new fields is the tricky part that America didn’t figure out during its painful deindustrialisation. Governments, companies and nonprofits are trying to learn from that failure. If that didn’t jolt you awake a cup of coffee might, but a cup of joe could become a luxury as climate change threatens coffee-growing regions. 1843, our sister magazine, profiles a scientist trying to save your morning brew in the surprisingly buccaneering world of wild coffee. Lane Greene, Senior digital editor What to expect in the week ahead: ▸ On Tuesday SpaceX will release its first quarterly results since its record-breaking IPO, providing markets with an insight into the financial health of the rockets-and-AI company. The firm’s value soared to $2.1trn in June, before slumping amid wider concerns about long-term profitability in AI-related stocks. ▸ Democrats in Michigan will vote in the party’s Senate primary on Tuesday. Abdul El-Sayed, a left-winger critical of the Democratic establishment, is facing up against Haley Stevens, a moderate who once worked for Barack Obama. The race is vital to Democrats’ hopes of winning a Senate majority and frustrating Donald Trump’s legislative agenda. But the contest is also important for determining which ideological faction will control the party going forward.  ▸ Markets and central bankers in America will be monitoring the release of key employment data on Friday. The Bureau of Labour Statistics is set to report on the growth of non-farm payrolls in July after an unexpected loss of momentum in the previous month. This followed an otherwise strong year so far. An uptick in jobs could mean growing pressure on Kevin Warsh, the Federal Reserve chair, to raise interest rates. Editor’s picks  Can America retrain workers before AI leaves them behind?
